reader.requirement: At --std 85 the compiler must accept, in an FD, LINAGE [IS] {data-name-1 | integer-1} [LINES] [[WITH] FOOTING [AT] {data-name-2 | integer-2}] [[LINES] [AT] TOP {data-name-3 | integer-3}] [[LINES] [AT] BOTTOM {data-name-4 | integer-4}] in that phrase order, each operand a (qualifiable) data-name or an unsigned integer literal that is nonzero for integer-1/integer-2 (§1985:III.2) and may be zero for integer-3/integer-4 (SR4), and refuse missing, zero, signed, decimal, nonnumeric, figurative or reordered/repeated operands; the witness covers qualified data-name operands only.

edition-consulted.switches: zero refusal of integer-1/integer-2 cites §1985:III.2 below 2002 (message only; the Nonzero/Zero slots are the same at every edition)
LinageClauseRules.Operand/Footing: the SR1/SR3 refusals cite the 1985 designation at --std 85 (message only)
the constant-name arm (_host.Constants.ConstantOf) is reachable only where constant entries exist (2002+); at 85 every word operand takes the data-name arm

reader.edition-search: grep 1985/Edition in FileControlBinder.FileSection.cs, FileControlBinder.Resolve.cs, LinageClauseRules.cs; grep Linage in IntegerOperandPass.cs and VersionConformancePass*.cs (no LINAGE gate); the four grammar rules carry no predicate.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the format shape and operand narrowing are the same code at 85 and 2023; only the cited rule designations change, and a constant-name operand exists only from 2002.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness exercises qualified data-name operands; the literal forms, optional-word omissions, zero rules for each phrase and the order/refusal half are not exercised by it
